en: The Questions of King Milinda: The Chapter on Similes, Section on the Earth "Venerable sir, just as the great earth, though it receives all manner of impurities—whether filth or what is not filth—yet remains neither defiled nor stained, so too, venerable sir, does the mind of the Tathāgata remain neither defiled nor stained, even when he receives all manner of insults and abuse from those who are hostile and malevolent. "Great king, suppose there were a man who, having smeared his body with oil, were to enter a house and stand in the doorway. Then, if someone were to throw a handful of dust into that house, would that dust stick to him? "No, venerable sir. "And why not? "Because he is covered by oil; the dust cannot adhere to him. "In the same way, great king, the Tathāgata has long since washed away the stain of lust with the water of non-lust, the stain of hatred with the water of non-hatred, and the stain of delusion with the water of non-delusion. Therefore, even when he receives all manner of insults and abuse from those who are hostile and malevolent, his mind remains neither defiled nor stained. "Venerable sir, just as the great ocean is deep, immeasurable, unfathomable, and possesses a single taste—the taste of salt—so too, venerable sir, is the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One deep, immeasurable, unfathomable, and possesses a single taste—the taste of liberation. "Great king, suppose there were a man who, having gone to the great ocean, were to take a drop of water on the tip of a blade of kusa grass. Would he know whether that drop of water was much more or less than the water in the great ocean? "No, venerable sir. "And why not? "Because the great ocean is deep, immeasurable, unfathomable, and possesses a single taste—the taste of salt. "In the same way, great king, the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One is deep, immeasurable, unfathomable, and possesses a single taste—the taste of liberation. "Venerable sir, just as the great ocean does not overflow its boundaries, so too, venerable sir, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One does not overstep the training rules laid down by the Blessed One. "Great king, suppose there were a man who, having gone to the great ocean, were to measure its depth with a measuring rod. Even if he were to do so for a hundred years, he would not reach the bottom, let alone find its limit. Why is that? Because the great ocean is deep, immeasurable, and unfathomable. "In the same way, great king, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One does not overstep the training rules laid down by the Blessed One. "Venerable sir, just as the great ocean contains many precious gems, such as pearls, gems, lapis lazuli, conch shells, quartz, coral, silver, gold, rubies, and cat's-eye gems, so too, venerable sir, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One contains many precious gems, such as the Stream-enterer, the Once-returner, the Non-returner, and the Arahant. "Great king, suppose there were a man who, having gone to the great ocean, were to take one precious gem. Would he think: 'This is the greatest of the gems in the great ocean'? "No, venerable sir. "And why not? "Because the great ocean contains many precious gems. "In the same way, great king, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One contains many precious gems, such as the Stream-enterer, the Once-returner, the Non-returner, and the Arahant. "Venerable sir, just as the great ocean is the abode of great beings, such as the timi, timiṅgila, and other large fish, so too, venerable sir, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One is the abode of great beings, such as the Stream-enterer, the Once-returner, the Non-returner, and the Arahant. "Great king, suppose there were a man who, having gone to the great ocean, were to take a single drop of water. Would he think: 'This is the great ocean'? "No, venerable sir. "And why not? "Because the great ocean is vast and immense. "In the same way, great king, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One is vast and immense. "Venerable sir, just as the great ocean is the source of all rivers, so too, venerable sir, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One is the source of all noble attainments. "Great king, suppose there were a man who, having gone to the great ocean, were to take a drop of water. Would he think: 'This drop of water came from the great ocean'? "Yes, venerable sir. "In the same way, great king, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One is the source of all noble attainments. "Venerable sir, just as the great ocean is the abode of the Nāgas, so too, venerable sir, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One is the abode of the Nāgas of the Noble Ones. "Great king, suppose there were a man who, having gone to the great ocean, were to take a drop of water. Would he think: 'This drop of water belongs to the Nāgas'? "Yes, venerable sir. "In the same way, great king, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One is the abode of the Nāgas of the Noble Ones. "Venerable sir, just as the great ocean is the abode of the Garuḍas, so too, venerable sir, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One is the abode of the Garuḍas of the Noble Ones. "Great king, suppose there were a man who, having gone to the great ocean, were to take a drop of water. Would he think: 'This drop of water belongs to the Garuḍas'? "Yes, venerable sir. "In the same way, great king, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One is the abode of the Garuḍas of the Noble Ones.

"Venerable sir, just as the great ocean is the abode of the Asuras, so too, venerable sir, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One is the abode of the Asuras of the Noble Ones. "Great king, suppose there were a man who, having gone to the great ocean, were to take a drop of water. Would he think: 'This drop of water belongs to the Asuras'? "Yes, venerable sir. "In the same way, great king, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One is the abode of the Asuras of the Noble Ones. "Venerable sir, just as the great ocean is the abode of the Devas, so too, venerable sir, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One is the abode of the Devas of the Noble Ones. "Great king, suppose there were a man who, having gone to the great ocean, were to take a drop of water. Would he think: 'This drop of water belongs to the Devas'? "Yes, venerable sir. "In the same way, great king, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One is the abode of the Devas of the Noble Ones. "Venerable sir, just as the great ocean is the abode of the Brahmas, so too, venerable sir, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One is the abode of the Brahmas of the Noble Ones. "Great king, suppose there were a man who, having gone to the great ocean, were to take a drop of water. Would he think: 'This drop of water belongs to the Brahmas'? "Yes, venerable sir. "In the same way, great king, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One is the abode of the Brahmas of the Noble Ones. "Venerable sir, just as the great ocean is the abode of the Great Beings, so too, venerable sir, the community of bhikkhus established by the Blessed One is the abode of the Great Beings of the Noble Ones. "Great king, suppose there were a man who, having gone to the great ocean, were to take a drop of water. Would he think: 'This drop of water belongs to the Great Beings'? "Yes, venerable sir. 3. The Question on the Factors of Fire “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘five factors of fire should be adopted,’ which are those five factors that should be adopted?
“Just as fire, O King, burns up grass, wood, branches, and foliage;”

In the same way, Great King, whatever internal or external defilements there may be for a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, which experience desirable or undesirable objects—all these must be consumed by the fire of knowledge.
This, Great King, is the first quality of fire that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, fire is merciless and pitiless.
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga should not show compassion or pity toward any of the defilements.
This, Great King, is the second quality of fire that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, fire repels cold.
In the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, having generated the heat of the energy of effort, should repel the defilements.
This, great king, is the third quality of fire that should be adopted.
Furthermore, great king, fire, being free from both attraction and aversion, generates heat.
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga, being free from attraction and aversion, should dwell with a mind like fire.
This, Great King, is the fourth quality of fire that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, fire dispels darkness and reveals light.
In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga, the yogāvacara, having dispelled the darkness of ignorance, should manifest the light of knowledge.
This, Great King, is the fifth quality of fire that should be adopted.
And this, Great King, was spoken by the Blessed One, the God above gods, while exhorting his own son Rāhula:
“Rāhula, develop the meditation that is like fire.
For while you are developing the meditation that is like fire, Rāhula, arisen agreeable and disagreeable contacts will not persist by obsessing the mind.
This is the third question on the fire element.
